title: LIN-4347 second tidy-after: the run store knows less about leftovers; the two repos agree by test, not prose
description:
## As asked

Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour), and JKershaw/simple-dispatcher.

**What this is for.** The leftover step and area notes (LIN-4347), their fix (LIN-4375) and their first tidy-after (LIN-4376) are working live. Read blind as one area across both repos (LinearViewer `526bca66..110e35e0`, simple-dispatcher `4aee0c9f`, `cb79e000`), both readers still call it mixed. It's the first area this week where a tidy-after didn't turn it better. Both credit the series for picking up after itself. Both say most of the cost landed where it shouldn't, and that the line between the two repos is held only by prose.

What both readers named:

* **The run store carries the leftover step.** `lib/dispatch-store.js` grew from 4,129 to 4,540 lines with hold, claim and release logic, and the shared wake delivery threads a leftover-only `release` flag through its guard branches. One area note now says the code should stay there. A note that defends a choice is worth re-reading, not obeying: if a seam where the store asks about held wakes without knowing the word "leftover" can be cut cleanly, cut it and update the note. If it can't, say why in the note's own words.
* **The two repos agree only in prose.** The notes README has already drifted between them. simple-dispatcher's `links.js` has a second `DONE:` matcher beside `hook.js`'s, anchored differently, and a second join of tool calls to results beside `walkToolActivity`. "The session's own PR" (`sessionPrs` and `reportedPrUrlOf`) is tied together only by comments. Where a shared example or one test across both repos would catch drift cheaply, add it. Where it wouldn't pay, say so.
* **Smaller misses:** `leftoverClaimedAt` isn't declared where sparse fields are declared. The registry's path constant lives in the research scripts, although the product owns the registry, so a product test helper imports from scripts. `lib/pipeline-churn.js` writes `'leftover'` as a literal. A stuck-wake case (a claim with no row) is noted but not fixed.

The prompt-byte growth (6.5 KB) belongs to the rule-folding ticket, LIN-4350, not here.

These are claims from readers, not facts, so look first and drop any that don't hold.

**Appetite:** err larger, within this area. Where a piece of tidying turns out not to pay, stop and say so.

**Done looks like:** the run store knows less about leftovers, the two repos can't drift on the things they must agree on without a test noticing, and the area reads simpler than LIN-4376 left it.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Implementation Plan

*Discharged. The approved plan is preserved word for word in the task snapshots (for example the one captured 2026-11-08T12:45:39Z) and in the comment trail.* The plan was sized as **needs multiple sessions**: Part A in one LinearViewer PR, and Part B as a LinearViewer PR followed by a simple-dispatcher PR.

plan-review due: yes

## Implemented (close-out, 2026-11-08)

What was built, all merged, deployed, and with CI green on each merge commit:

* **Part A — LIN-4383**, [LinearViewer #2366](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2366>) (`f8b946d40`). The run store keeps generic held-wake primitives keyed on `heldWakeFor`, and the leftover policy and outcome-wake wording moved to `lib/dispatch-leftover-hook.js`. The store has zero code lines matching /leftover/i, and the `lin-4377-store-knows-no-leftover` census enforces that. `HELD_WAKE_CLAIMED_AT` is declared with the sparse fields. The registry path lives in the product leaf `lib/prompts/area-registry-path.js`. The area note states the new boundary.
* **Part B1 — LIN-4384**, [LinearViewer #2365](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2365>) (`936f52b7d`). Adds `report` and `sentinel` rows to the runner contract, a per-area shape check and a sha256 tripwire.
* **Part B2 — LIN-4385**, [simple-dispatcher #332](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/332>) (`59a0dc2`). Adds a byte-identical copy of the contract, driven by SD's own readers, with one `DONE:` rule and one tool-call/result join in `transcript.js`. The README now points to Harbour's `LEFTOVER_RULE`.
* **Operator follow-up** to LIN-4383: [LinearViewer #2368](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2368>) (`32da8d583`) and [simple-dispatcher #333](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/333>) (`8093c17`). These give a degraded release one log prefix and add Waiting entries to the area notes.

**Plan fidelity:** implemented as approved. Each deviation is recorded in that part's comment on this ticket:

* Part A adds `heldWakeProducerOf`, which keeps the same single read.
* In B2, the README pointer names where Harbour renders the rule.
* B2's shared join also joins results that come before their uses, and keeps only the last result for a repeated ID.

**Accepted limit, ruled in "Size of the move":** contract drift is caught in one direction only.

**Still open:** the operator's post-deploy Railway log checks, not run and recorded in the close-out comment. The stuck claim-with-no-row case stays under Waiting in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`.

Full plan, research findings and stage history are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

## Survey global: LIN-4377 @ 110e35e05

(LinearViewer `110e35e05`; simple-dispatcher `cb79e0009`.)

**Where it lands.** Mostly `lib/dispatch-store.js`, which went from 4,129 to 4,540 lines across the series. It mentions "leftover" 79 times. The claims hold. The hook is already injected (`leftoverHook`, `lib/dispatch-leftover-hook.js`), so the seam half exists. But the store still owns `_applyLeftoverStep` (it rewrites the wake prompt with the build's outcome), `_heldLeftoverOf`, the claim pair, `findLeftoverRows`, and a `LEFTOVER_KIND` clause in the stopped-run cleanup.

**The note's defence is weaker than it reads.** "Three guards read `release`" is true, but what `release` means has nothing to do with leftovers. It means *there's no re-report to retry, so degrade rather than withdraw*. Rename it for that meaning (`noRetry`, say) and let the caller pick the log tag, and `_deliverWake` no longer knows the word. "A module handed the store only exposes its privates" is true only if the store is handed over whole. The hook already takes `dispatchStore`, so the prompt-rewrite half of `_applyLeftoverStep` can move into the hook as a richer verdict (`{outcome:'rewrite', wakeFollowUp}` beside `queued`/`hold`). Then the store keeps three generic things: a held-wake field (`heldWakeFor` already has a neutral name), a CAS stamp, and `releaseHeldWake`. The cleanup can match `heldWakeFor: {$exists}` instead of the kind. Rename `leftoverClaimedAt` to a held-wake claim and declare it in the sparse-key list of `lib/dispatch-fields.js`, which names sparse keys in prose. The `'leftover'` literal in `pipeline-churn.js` sits among `'implementation'` literals, so swapping it alone doesn't pay.

**Cross-repo agreement.** The READMEs differ mostly where they should, but the leftover rule really has drifted. LinearViewer moved it into `LEFTOVER_RULE` (`lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`). simple-dispatcher's README still carries an older prose copy, and Harbour's prompts render the real rule on simple-dispatcher tasks anyway. Delete that copy and point to Harbour's rule in prose. No test is needed there.

The PR-of-run rule is the contract worth a test: `reportedPrUrlOf`/`reportLinesOf` against `sessionPrs`/`selectCanonical`. The repos share no code, but they already have a precedent held by prose: `TICKET_MARKER_LINE` in `transcript.js`. Put one small shared fixture (message → expected PR, including the two-PRs-on-one-line case) in both repos. Each repo's test checks its own reader against the fixture and pins the fixture's hash, so editing one copy without the other fails CI. That's cheap.

Inside simple-dispatcher: `DONE_LINE_RE` scans every assistant block, including `DONE:` inside DECISION/WITHDRAW JSON, which `hook.js` warns about. `parseCompletionSentinel` reads trimmed lines of the last turn only. Fix both with one exported line rule from a module both files can import (`links.js` can't import `hook.js`). The second tool-use/result join could become a `toolCallsWithResults` exported from `transcript.js` that `walkToolActivity` and `sessionPrs` both read.

Move it next to the product (into a `lib/` module, or have the helper own it) and have scripts import it. The stuck claim with no row is a sweep, a new job, and it touches the queue TTL. Leave it in Waiting unless the seam move lands cleanly.

**Not this task's.** Splitting the store beyond leftovers, and a shared package between the repos.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4377 @ 110e35e05

LinearViewer `110e35e05`; simple-dispatcher `cb79e0009`. Every smaller claim holds: `leftoverClaimedAt` has no entry beside `heldWakeForOf` in `lib/dispatch-fields.js`; `tests/unit/helpers/area-registry.js` imports `REGISTRY_PATH` from `scripts/code-shape/code-shape-lib.mjs`; `lib/pipeline-churn.js` writes `'leftover'` although `LEFTOVER_KIND` exists; the stuck wake is still listed under Waiting. The store did grow 4,129 → 4,540, with 61 lines that say "leftover".

**Why it's hard**

1. **The note's reason mixes up the flag's name with what it means.** It says "no move takes `release` out of `_deliverWake` (three of its guards read it)". But all three guards apply one rule that has nothing to do with leftovers: *no re-report will retry this, so degrade instead of withdrawing*. That's a delivery policy (call it `retryable: false`), and the store can own it without knowing the word. The same goes for `heldWakeFor`, which is already a general name, and for the claim, which is the `_mintWake` compare-and-set idiom on one field. What is truly leftover-specific is small: the `kind === LEFTOVER_KIND` checks in `_heldLeftoverOf` and the cancel sweep, the log tags, and `_applyLeftoverStep`'s outcome-wake text. The trap is a shuffle that moves lines into a new module and calls the store smaller. Judge success by what the store knows (count the word), not by its line count. The wake guards are also order-sensitive and pinned by two censuses (`lin-3134`, `lin-4080`). Rename inside `_deliverWake` and leave its shape alone.

2. **"Agree only in prose" is partly wrong. A test mechanism already exists and nobody named it.** LIN-3451's `lib/runner-kit/contract.json` is byte-copied to simple-dispatcher's `test/fixtures/runner-contract.json` with a sha256 pin, and both sides' tests drive it. Extend that instead of inventing a second channel. Its limit: a Harbour-side edit isn't noticed until someone re-copies, so it catches drift in one direction only. Say that plainly.

3. **There are four `DONE:` matchers, not two:** `parseCompletionSentinel` in `hook.js` (trimmed, first line wins), `DONE_LINE_RE` in `links.js` (every line, `^\s*`), `REPORT_LINE_RE` in `lib/dispatch-terminal.js` (also matches `[done]`), and `OUTCOME_LINE` in `runner.mjs` (last non-empty line, no indent). They answer different questions (is the turn over? which line names a PR?), so merging them would be wrong. Pin the shared cases as contract rows instead: an indented `DONE:`, two `DONE:` lines, two PRs on one line, a `DONE:` inside a DECISION block. The last one could genuinely diverge today.

4. **Some of it won't pay.** A cross-repo test on README prose costs more than the drift it catches. A cheaper fix: simple-dispatcher's leftover section stops restating the routes and points, in prose, to Harbour's `LEFTOVER_RULE`, which already renders into its prompts. In simple-dispatcher, folding `sessionPrs`'s tool join into `walkToolActivity` means splitting a raw join out of it first. That's cheap, but `stop-relay-order.golden.json` guards it.

**The deeper issue:** the store is the only place with transactional primitives, so every feature that needs a compare-and-set lands there. The leftover step is the latest of these, not the cause.

**What I'd do first:** rename `release` to the policy it is. Then see whether `_heldLeftoverOf` and the cancel sweep can key on `heldWakeFor` instead of on kind. If both work, everything else can move behind the already-injected `leftoverHook`, and the note can be rewritten. Design the stuck-wake sweep in the same pass: it reads the claim and the rows, so where it lives tests the seam. Then add the contract rows.

## Size of the move (the person's call)

Err larger, John's standing answer. Both Surveys checked every claim, and both found the note that defends the store's leftover code weaker than it reads.

**The run store stops knowing about leftovers.** The `release` flag means "no re-report will retry this, so degrade rather than withdraw". That's a delivery policy with nothing to do with leftovers. Name it for what it means, and leave the shape of the wake delivery alone, because its order-sensitive guards are pinned by the censuses. The held-wake lookup and the stopped-run cleanup can key on `heldWakeFor`, which is already a general name, instead of on the run's kind. The claim is the usual compare-and-set on one field: give it a held-wake name and declare it with the other sparse fields. What's truly leftover-specific, such as the text of the outcome wake, can move behind the leftover hook, which is already injected. Measure success by what the store knows, not by lines moved: count how often it says "leftover". Then rewrite the area note in its own words, to say what's now true. If the cleanup of a claim with no row fits the seam, design it in the same pass. If not, it stays under Waiting.

**The two repos agree by test where it pays.** A mechanism already exists: the runner contract (`lib/runner-kit/contract.json`), byte-copied into simple-dispatcher's fixtures with a hash pin, and driven by tests on both sides. Extend it rather than invent a second channel. Add the cases the two sides must read the same way: which PR a run opened (including two PRs on one line), an indented `DONE:`, two `DONE:` lines, and a `DONE:` inside a DECISION block, which may genuinely diverge today. The four `DONE:` matchers answer different questions, so pin the shared cases rather than merging them. Say plainly that the copy catches drift in one direction only. In simple-dispatcher, the notes README stops restating the leftover rule and points to Harbour's, which already reaches its prompts. Where `hook.js` and `links.js` need the same line rule, give them one they can both import. Do the tool-call join only if its golden file allows it cheaply.

**Smaller:** the registry's path constant moves to the product side, and the scripts import it from there. Swapping the `pipeline-churn` literal on its own doesn't pay, so drop it.

**Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself, and record why. Raise a ruling only for John's calls.

**Done when** the store's leftover knowledge is clearly smaller by that count, the wake delivery says nothing about leftovers, the shared cases are pinned by the contract on both sides, and the area reads simpler than LIN-4376 left it.

## Investigation: kickoff sessions get 502 from the local broker

**Short answer:** this was not a credential failure. Both exchanges got **HTTP 429 from Harbour's shared per-IP limiter** (`proxyLimiter`, 60 per minute), which answers before the exchange handler runs. Another session on the same host was using up that budget with a bulk crawl. The broker hid the 429 behind a generic 502.

### 1. Harbour (Railway HTTP logs, `harbour-cat`, deployment `7529e78c`)
- **LIN-4349** (session `85ee4d57`, started 08:25:22): `POST /api/proxy/token` got **429** at 08:25:33, :35 and :38.
- **LIN-4377** (session `9c45153f`, started 08:28:49): **429** at 08:29:01, :04 and :07.
- Each 429 took 1–2 ms and had a 59-byte body, `proxyLimiter`'s exact message (`routes/proxy.js:237`). The exchange route sits behind it (`routes/proxy-token-exchange.js:38`).
- No lineage, grant, owner or expiry reason exists: the handler never ran.
- **Exchanges that worked in the same hour:** 08:24:50, 08:25:09 (custom item `cccb31b2`), 08:28:09 and 08:29:25, all 200. They arrived while budget remained. Lane made no difference.

### 2. Runner and broker
- Both items arrived **with a bootstrap**. The run log shows "broker armed", and the LIN-1446 fallback line appears nowhere in it.
- `exchange returned HTTP …` is **never logged**: `forwardProxyRequest` drops the error (`harbour-token-mcp-server.js:226-229`).
- Both bootstraps are **unspent**, because a 429 comes before the handler. Both brokers are still alive.

### 3. Mint path, and why it broke at a point in time
- `LANES.kickoff` declares `dispatch` with `grantOwnerAccountId = req.proxyCreatedBy` (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js:844`). `mintGrantBootstrap` mints a 48h `worker` bootstrap (`lib/proxy-preamble.js:568`).
- Both kickoffs returned **201**. A problem with runner-copy lifetimes (1h/24h) or a lineage revoke would have shown as a 401, not a 429.
- **What changed was traffic, not code.** `GET /api/proxy/dispatch` from the host's single IP went from 0 per minute (07:20) to about 24 per minute from **07:44:46**, then about 100 per minute by 07:58 and about 150 by 08:20. At that rate the budget runs out a few seconds after each reset, and everything from the host gets 429 until the next one. In 08:20–08:31 the host took 134 `GET /dispatch` 429s, plus 429s on reads, comments and `recommend-and-dispatch`.
- **The source is session `6bd0eee6`** (LIN-4376 item `bb36e706`, launched 07:40). Its scratchpad `rt-fetch.mjs` (07:44) and `rt-fetch2.mjs` crawl all 4,315 issues: two workers call `GET /dispatch?issueIdentifier=…` once per issue, and they **retry on 429**. A stall-failsafe resume at 08:29 restarted it. Its log was still advancing at 08:51.

### 4. What else is at risk
- **Any fresh launch or refire on this host** while the crawl runs. Its exchange is a coin-flip against the limiter.
- Sessions already holding a working token keep it, but still get 429s.
- The runner's poll (`/api/dispatch/poll`) is a different route and was unaffected.

### Most likely cause, evidence, what to do
**Cause:** a bulk crawl in `6bd0eee6` used up the per-IP limiter, and the single-use exchange shares that limiter. **Evidence:**
- the 429 timestamps fall 10–20 s after each session started;
- the 59-byte limiter body;
- the 07:44:46 onset matches `rt-fetch.mjs`;
- both kickoffs returned 201 and both bootstraps are unspent.

**To do:**
1. Stop the `6bd0eee6` crawl, or let it finish.
2. Send a follow-up to `85ee4d57` and `9c45153f`: their brokers will retry the same bootstrap, which is still valid for up to 48h. Re-dispatching also works.
3. As a follow-up, take `/api/proxy/token` out from behind the shared data limiter, and make the broker retry a 429 with backoff.

**What would have told us sooner:** the broker passing on `429 rate-limited (Retry-After)` instead of a bare 502, and logging `exchange returned HTTP 429` to the oplog.

## Research: LIN-4377 @ LinearViewer `110e35e0`, simple-dispatcher `cb79e00`

Neither repo has a commit since the ticket was filed (`git log --since=2026-11-08T08:24:30Z` is empty in both), so the Surveys' line references still hold. I built on the two Surveys and John's "Size of the move". Their claims were tested with two throwaway spikes, one per repo, run against the real suites. Nothing was pushed.

### What the spikes proved

**Store seam (LinearViewer).** I applied the selected approach in a scratch worktree:
- renamed `release` to `retryable: false`;
- keyed held-wake lookup and the stopped-run cleanup on `heldWakeFor`;
- renamed the claim pair and the timestamp field;
- made `findLeftoverRows` generic (kind passed in);
- moved `_applyLeftoverStep`'s outcome-wake rewrite into the hook as a `rewrite` verdict;
- renamed the hook's `queued`/`hold` answers to `withhold`.

Results:
- **Full unit suite: 24,324 / 24,324 pass**, including `lin-3134-declared-mint-census`, `lin-4080-addItem-census`, `lin-3805-store-fault-503`, `key-state-census` and every wake suite.
- **Test edits needed:** 4 spots, all renames or log tags. No assertion about behaviour changed.
- **"leftover" in `lib/dispatch-store.js`:** 79 → 39 lines, case-insensitive (93 → 43 occurrences). **Code lines went from 40 to 0.** The 39 left are comments, which the implementer rewrites. The real target is 0 code lines and a handful of comment pointers to the hook.
- Store 4,540 → 4,524 lines, hook 184 → 211. As the Survey warned, line counts are not the measure.

**simple-dispatcher.** In a scratch worktree I extracted `toolCallsWithResults` and `doneLineRest` into `transcript.js`. `walkToolActivity`, `sessionPrs` and `parseCompletionSentinel` now read them.
- **Full suite: 4,270 pass, 5 skipped, 0 fail.** That includes `stop-relay-order-characterization` (the golden), `lin-4375-session-pr`, `links` and `transcript`.

**Cross-repo readers.** I fed 13 message shapes through all four readers: Harbour `prUrlOfFeedback`/`reportLinesOf`, SD `sessionPrs`/`parseCompletionSentinel`, and the kit's `transcriptFinished`.

| case | Harbour PR (report line) | SD `sessionPrs` | SD sentinel | kit finished |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| one DONE line, one PR | #2360 | #2360 | done | true |
| two PRs on one DONE line | first | first | done | true |
| indented `DONE:` | read | read | done | true |
| two DONE lines | **newest** (#2) | **newest** (#2) | done, *first* line | true |
| DONE inside a DECISION block, real DONE after | #3 | #3 | done, *first* (#9) | true |
| **DONE only inside a DECISION block** | #9 | #9 | **done** | **false** |
| DONE mid-line | none (falls back to any URL) | none | none | false |
| `[done]` marker line | read | not read | none | false |
| PR URL with `/files` | `/pull/12` | `/pull/12` | done | true |

What the table shows:
- **The two PR readers agree on every report-line case today**, including `DONE:` inside a DECISION block: both read it.
- So the Survey's "may genuinely diverge" holds, but between **SD's hook and the kit** (is the turn over?), not between the PR readers.
- Making `links.js` skip DECISION blocks on its own would **create** a cross-repo divergence: SD relays the whole assistant text (`postAssistantTextDelta`, `hook.js`), so Harbour still sees those lines.
- That is the drift a contract row should catch. Pin today's agreement. Don't change one side.

### Per-layer audit

**L1. `_deliverWake` (lib/dispatch-store.js).**
- Today `release` is read in four places, not three: the declaration-lookup catch, the no-provisioner log, `reason && release`, and the `[leftover] release-degraded` log tags inside them.
- All four apply one policy: *no re-report will retry, so degrade rather than withdraw*.
- The order and shape are pinned by the two censuses (`tests/unit/lin-4080-addItem-census.test.js` names `_deliverWake` as the unguarded `[pending]` writer; `lin-3134-declared-mint-census` scans mint sites).
- Callers: `addFeedback` and `releaseHeldWake` (grep `_deliverWake(`).
- The rename to `retryable` (default `true`) plus a `[dispatch-wake] no-retry-degraded` tag keeps the shape byte-for-byte apart from names. The spike passed both censuses unchanged.

**L2. `_applyLeftoverStep` (dispatch-store.js:3403).**
- It does two things:
  1. On a non-`[done]` terminal, or a `[pending]`, in a holder's lineage, it rewrites the wake with the build's outcome.
  2. It calls the hook and applies `queued`/`hold`.
- Part 1 is the only leftover wording in the store (`formatLeftoverPendingNote`, plus `formatHeldWakeNote({marker})`).
- `addFeedback` has exactly two production callers, `routes/proxy-runner.js:223` and `routes/dispatch.js:1628` (grep `\.addFeedback(`), and both pass the hook. So moving part 1 into the hook has no hookless production consumer.
- The tests drive the real hook (`world.hook`, `tests/unit/lin-4373-leftover-step.test.js:60`), so every part-1 case still runs.
- The hook now runs for `[pending]` too. It must return quietly there, without adding a `[leftover] skipped` line to every pending wake. The spike does this.

**L3. `_heldLeftoverOf` (dispatch-store.js:3476).**
